questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

William ______ his friends not to intrude into his family’s affairs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**warned'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word for the given blank is '**warned**'.
 
• It means **'to tell somebody about something unpleasant or dangerous that exists or might happen, so that he/she can avoid it'.** [(किसी व्‍यक्ति को) आसन्‍न, विद्यमान प्रतिकूलता या ख़तरे की पूर्वसूचना देना, (से) सचेत करना (ताकि वह अपना बचाव कर सके)]
 
 
• *Example: When I saw the car coming I tried to **warn** him, but it was too late.*
 
 
 
• Let's look at the meaning of other words:
 
 
• **claimed**: to say that something is true, without having any proof. (बिना प्रमाण प्रस्‍तुत किए सत्‍यता का दावा करना)
 
• **gambled**: to bet money on the result of a card game, horse race, etc. (ताश का खेल, घुड़दौड़ आदि के परिणामों पर बाज़ी लगाना; जुआ खेलना)
 
• **satisfied**: pleased because you have had or done what you wanted. (अभीष्‍ट काम को संपन्‍न करने या वस्‍तु को प्राप्‍त करने पर प्रसन्‍न; संतुष्‍ट)
 
 
 
• Thus, as per the above definitions, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *William **warned** his friends not to intrude into his family's affairs.*

While the symptoms __are troubling,__ they typically resolve within two weeks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No improvement required'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• Here, all the grammatical rules are being followed.
 
• The **present continuous tense** is a grammatical tense that can be used to describe when an action happened or may happen.
 
• We can use it to describe both events that are happening in the present – right now, while we are talking about something, or in the future – something that may or will happen later on. 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *While the symptoms** are troubling**, they typically resolve within two weeks.*

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

I don’t know anyone who spoken Portuguese in my school.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'who spoken Portuguese'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'who speaks Portuguese'** should be used instead of** 'who spoken Portuguese'.**
 
• In the given sentence '**who**' is **a relative pronoun.**
 
• We know that the verb after it should be used according to its **antecedent**. 
 
• Here, its antecedent is '**anyone**'. So, accordingly, a singular helping verb that is '**speaks**' should be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Correct Sentence:__** *I don't know anyone **who speaks Portuguese **in my school.*

• **critically**: in a way that expresses disapproval. (नाज़ुक तौर पर, संकटग्रस्‍त रूप से)
 
• **radically**: in a thorough or fundamental way; completely. (आमूल, मूल रूप से, मूलतः)
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 2.**

 

**​**​____Correct Passage:__ *Every evening, at a point midway along the arrow-straight road between Amritsar and Lahore, rival squads of splendidly uniformed soldiers strut and stomp a 17th-century British military drill known as Beating Retreat.
